leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members prefer B018 as a single-part prize for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, with the same three names in every configuration. Shared: the theory-to-experiment arc (Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall prediction, then edge transport in HgTe quantum wells), roughly two decades of independent confirmation, and the view that it is mature. Not shared: citation wording. Danielsson and Johansson use a general 'prediction and experimental discovery/observation' form, while Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and the chair name HgTe quantum wells explicitly, which narrows the claim to the 2D case. All six also record the same credit gap, namely that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased) and the 3D work (Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan) fall outside the trio, and none of them treats this as disqualifying. Several supporters moved to B018 from other first choices in round 1 (Danielsson from B045, Johansson from B020, Mehlig from B032, the chair from B016), so support reflects convergence and not only the opening first places.

Two members prefer B041 as a single-part prize for Katori and Ye, with identical names and near-identical citations built on the magic-wavelength lattice and fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. Shared: the two-name credit is clean, performance has been reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg in several laboratories and checked by fibre-link comparisons, and the new capability is the case rather than a new phase of matter. Both also name the same objection themselves: possible overlap with the 2005 (comb) and 2012 (ion control and clocks) prizes, and fundamental-physics output so far limited to constraints. Both keep B018 as an alternative. They differ in how much weight they give to the unresolved priority question among Katori, Ye and the PTB, SYRTE, NIST and RIKEN groups.

areas_of_agreement: Six members prefer B018 and two prefer B041. Each B018 supporter lists B041 as an alternative, and Kroll and Lindroth list B018 as their first alternative, so each camp explicitly acknowledges the other's candidate.
The three-person Kane, Mele, Molenkamp credit for B018 is stated identically by all six of its supporters; no member proposes a different trio or a fourth name.
Both leading candidates are regarded as mature and independently reproduced; no member calls either premature.

Every member who discusses B018 records the same attribution caveat (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological insulator work), so the committee already has a shared list of what the citation must be careful about.

Several members (Mehlig, Olsson, Eriksson) state that opening support counts are not themselves a measure of merit, and several (the chair, Johansson, Lindroth, Eriksson) acknowledge expertise limits outside their own fields.
scientific_disputes: Whether B018 is a distinct discovery or a refinement of the topological-phase ideas recognised in 2016 (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz); raised by Mehlig and the chair, and not addressed by the other supporters.

Whether B041 is a new discovery or a very successful second-generation improvement in frequency metrology following the 2005 and 2012 prizes; raised by Kroll, Lindroth, Danielsson and Johansson, with its fundamental-physics output so far consisting of constraints and null results.

Whether the HgTe experiment is an independent discovery or the realisation of the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (Mehlig, Olsson); related to this, whether the practical impact of B018 is too limited and the HgTe edge quantisation too imperfect in longer samples.
Eriksson notes that condensed-matter members may favour B018 more than members can judge against atomic-physics or astrophysics candidates; the committee has no stated measure of how to weigh that.
attribution_disputes: B018: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the platform and Zhang died in 2018; Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents and Hasan carry the 3D case. Members differ on whether a citation limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 insulators is a fair account (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Johansson, the chair) or is arbitrary and fragmentary, and some members note their recollection of priority is from memory and unverified.

B041: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal versus Ye's performance frontier and the parallel contributions of Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow, Hinkley and the PTB, SYRTE, NIST/JILA and RIKEN groups (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson).
B016: a sole credit to Halzen for a collaboration of hundreds is not defensible (Danielsson, the chair); this is why it remains an alternative only.

B020 and B032 are alternatives for single members and carry attribution problems the proponents themselves flag: five credited names for B020 with at most three possible, and contested priority among Evans, Gallavotti, Cohen, Jarzynski, Crooks, Kurchan and Seifert for B032.
maturity_disputes: No member argues that B018 is premature; the question is whether it is arguably overdue (Eriksson, Mehlig) or simply secure.
B041: whether a prize on measurement method should wait for the redefinition of the second or is already mature (Kroll).
B016: the NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane source evidence rests on few events and has not been confirmed at comparable significance by KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD (Danielsson, the chair's own earlier concerns).
B030 (kept as an alternative by Eriksson and Olsson): whether the superconducting pairing mechanism needs to be settled first, or broad reproduction is enough (Eriksson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and embedded in the Chalmers superconducting-circuit community; says he should not take a lead role on B020 and also notes contact with the 2025 laureates as guest researchers at Chalmers.

Kroll: group works on laser stabilization with spectral-hole-burning crystals, a neighbouring technique to clock-laser technology and not a collaboration with Katori or Ye; also institutional links to WACQT/Chalmers and the quantum-memory community, which he says would warrant recusal or caution on B020 and quantum-information candidates.
Danielsson: no conflict on B018, B041 or B016; says he would recuse if a candidate with a direct Uppsala connection arose.
Mehlig and Olsson note that they share the Gothenburg (GU and Chalmers) environment with Johansson, and Olsson and Mehlig state no collaboration with any credited name.
Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and the chair report no specific conflict with the credited names on their preferred configurations.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee agree on B018 citation wording that fixes the scope (2D quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with HgTe named, or a broader topological insulator claim including 3D) and still treat the omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Hasan as a defensible attribution choice? Should the experts check the primary papers on whether BHZ was the decisive step for the HgTe experiment?

How does the 2016 prize (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) bear on B018: does it leave room for a distinct, experimentally established time-reversal-invariant topological insulator prize, and can Mehlig and the chair's concern be answered by the condensed-matter members?

For B041, what separates optical lattice clocks from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and who held priority and decisive contribution among Katori, Ye and the other groups? Can Kroll and Lindroth state a citation that makes the lattice concept the discovery and not the clock performance?

Does any member who ranked B018 first or second prefer a two-part prize pairing B018 with another candidate (the chair and Lindroth raised a precision-measurement pairing), and if so how would the three-laureate limit be honoured for both parts?
If B020 is advanced at all, which three of Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff, and how should Johansson's disclosed ties and the one-year gap after the 2025 prize be handled?
Can any member who has not ranked B018 first (Kroll, Lindroth) say whether the B018 case changes their ordering, and what evidence would move the B041 supporters?
summary.chair_observation: The explicit round-1 configurations are concentrated: six members prefer B018 with the same three names, two prefer B041 with the same two names, and no other candidate is a first choice in a preferred configuration. The B018 supporters came from varied opening positions and several moved on reading each other's ballots, so the next step is to test how robust that convergence is rather than to treat it as settled. The main open work is the wording and scope of the B018 citation and the novelty question for B041, not a dispute over who the laureates would be. Several members rely on recollection of priority history, so expert verification would help before the final ballot.
